mainTopic: Judging mixtures by taste or majority, imagining a same-kind mixture as a different kind, and רבי יהודה's 'red wine' test
overview: The גמרא gives a new explanation of ריש לקיש: when one kind is mixed with a different kind, we go by taste (טעמא), and when a kind is mixed with its own kind, we go by majority (רובא). It then suggests that even a same-kind mixture should be judged as if the two things were different. It tries to prove this from the משנה about blood mixed with wine, which we 'view as if it is water.' Someone answers that it is the blood that is viewed as water, but the גמרא replies that the משנה would then simply have said 'בטל.' It adds support from רבי יהודה, who imagines white wine or milk in a bucket dipped in a מקוה as if it were red wine. The proof is turned down, because in the same ברייתא the first opinion simply follows the majority, so this is a dispute of תנאים. The גמרא then raises a contradiction within רבי יהודה's own view. A משנה about immersing buckets uses his 'רואין' language for urine, yet for מי חטאת it says a simple majority is enough. אביי begins to answer that this is not difficult, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Different kinds go by taste, same kind goes by majority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new way to explain ריש לקיש. A mixture of different kinds is judged by taste. A mixture of the same kind is judged by majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a kind mixed with a different kind is judged by taste. A kind mixed with its own kind is judged by majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier explanation and offers a new one. Different kinds go by taste, and the same kind goes by majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא ("rather") tells us the earlier approach did not work. With two different kinds, you can taste which one is in charge, so taste decides. With the same kind, taste cannot tell them apart, so we go by which one is the majority. This fits ריש לקיש's case of פיגול mixed with נותר, which are both the same kind of meat.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this drops the earlier approach and brings a new one
A kind mixed with a different kind
A kind mixed with its own kind
Judged by taste
Judged by majority

steps.whatToRemember: There are two basic rules here. Different kinds are judged by taste (טעמא). The same kind is judged by majority (רובא).

phrases.english: Rather, a kind with what is not its kind: by taste;
a kind with its own kind: by majority.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces an earlier explanation of ריש לקיש from the previous part of the daf
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws a line between two kinds of mixtures
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One rule would apply to every mixture
steps.terutzMaskana: Taste decides for different kinds; majority decides for the same kind
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A different-kind mixture goes by taste; a same-kind mixture goes by majority

steps.title: Why not judge a same-kind mixture as if it were a different kind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that even for a same-kind mixture, we should imagine the two things are different and judge it that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us judge a kind mixed with its own kind as if it were a kind mixed with a different kind!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the majority rule. It suggests we should imagine the same-kind mixture as if the two things were different. It is setting up a proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we imagined the majority were a different substance, the minority might still be strong enough to be noticed. In that case it would not be nullified, even though it is the minority. This would undo the simple majority rule from step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us estimate or judge (by imagining)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the two things really are different kinds. It is suggesting we only imagine them that way as a way of measuring.

phrases.english: But let us estimate a kind with its own kind
as a kind with what is not its kind!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְשַׁעֵר מִין בְּמִינוֹ כְּמִין בְּשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges using the majority rule for same-kind mixtures
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a same-kind mixture is judged by majority
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We could imagine the majority as a different substance and check whether the minority would still be noticeable

steps.title: Proof from blood mixed with wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה about blood mixed with wine, where we view it 'as if it is water.' It suggests this means we imagine the wine as water.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: if it got mixed with wine, we view it as if it were water. Doesn't this mean we view the wine as if it were water?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its suggestion from a משנה. If blood got mixed with wine, we imagine the wine as water and check whether the blood would still show.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood and wine look alike, so in appearance they act like the same kind. The משנה says to view it 'as water,' and the גמרא reads this as imagining the wine as a different substance. That is exactly the method suggested in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: We view it as if
What, is it not...? (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.english: As we learned: if it was mixed with wine,
phrases.notes: "It" is the blood of a קרבן, from the משנה on the previous daf.

phrases.english: we view it as if it is water.
What, is it not that we view the wine
as if it is water?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to support the suggestion
steps.raayaObject: Judging a same-kind mixture as if it were a different kind
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about blood mixed with wine

steps.title: No, it is the blood we view as water
steps.stepSummary: The proof is turned down. The משנה means the blood itself is treated like water, which makes it unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: No; we view the blood as if it were water.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone rejects the proof. The משנה means the blood becomes like water, not the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read this way, the משנה is saying the blood is lost in the wine. Putting it on the מזבח would be like putting water there, so it is unfit. That reading gives no support to the 'imagine it as a different kind' method.

keyTerms.meaning: The blood (of the קרבן)

phrases.english: No; we view the blood
as if it is water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the משנה offered in step 3
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה, not the suggestion itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה could be talking about the blood, not the wine

steps.title: Then the משנה should have said 'nullified'
steps.stepSummary: The rejection is challenged. If the blood simply disappears, the משנה should have said 'בטל.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it should have said 'nullified'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the rejection. If the משנה meant the blood is simply lost, it would have said 'בטל.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'view it as water' is a roundabout way to say the blood is nullified. The longer wording suggests a real act of imagining, which means imagining the wine as water. So the original proof stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Nullified; lost in the mixture
He should have said

phrases.english: If so, it should have said "nullified"!

steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the blood is viewed as water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording does not fit simple nullification

steps.title: More support: רבי יהודה imagines white wine as red wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה. He says we imagine a substance as red wine, and if that red color would fade, it is fit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, it is taught: רבי יהודה says, we view it as if it were red wine. If its appearance would fade, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another source that supports the method of imagining. רבי יהודה imagines a pale liquid as red wine to judge whether it is lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a pale liquid is mixed with water, so you cannot see it at all. רבי יהודה imagines it as red wine to measure whether it would still show. This is the same kind of imagined test proposed in step 2. The quote finishes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore
Red wine
Its appearance faded
Fit; valid

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that imagining a substance with a different appearance is a real method used in הלכה. This strengthens the reading of the משנה from step 3.

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught:
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יַיִן אָדוֹם;
phrases.english: we view it as if it is red wine;
phrases.notes: "It" is a pale liquid, like white wine or milk, that mixed with מקוה water and cannot be seen.

phrases.english: if its appearance would fade, it is fit,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source after defending the first
steps.raayaObject: Judging a mixture by imagining a substance with a different appearance
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה about imagining red wine

steps.title: Finishing the red wine proof: if the color stays, it is unfit
steps.stepSummary: The last words of רבי יהודה's rule complete the proof. If the imagined red color would not fade, the immersion does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if not, it is unfit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the quote from step 6. With these words the proof is complete: if the imagined red wine would not fade, the immersion is unfit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: White wine and milk look a lot like water, much like a same-kind mixture. Yet רבי יהודה does not let them simply blend in. He imagines them as red wine, something that looks clearly different. That seems to back up the suggestion from step 2: even a same-kind mixture is judged as if the two things were different.

keyTerms.meaning: Unfit; here, the immersion does not work.
Fit; here, the immersion works.
A mixture of the same kind, or of things that look alike.

phrases.english: And if not, it is unfit!
phrases.notes: This finishes רבי יהודה's words from step 6. 'If not' means the imagined red color would not fade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 6, so the proof is now fully stated.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that a same-kind mixture is judged as if it were a different-kind mixture.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה in the ברייתא: imagine the white wine or milk as red wine. If the color would not fade, the immersion is unfit.

steps.title: The proof is turned down: it is a dispute of the early sages
steps.stepSummary: The proof from רבי יהודה does not hold. The same ברייתא shows that the חכמים disagree and simply follow the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים. As it is taught: a bucket that has white wine or milk in it, and he immersed it, we follow the majority. רבי יהודה says: we view it as if it were red wine. If its color would fade, it is fit, and if not, it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי יהודה's view is only one side of an argument between תנאים, so it cannot prove the general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא quotes the whole ברייתא again, this time to show its first opinion. The first, unnamed opinion says 'follow the majority', with no imagining of red wine. So the proof only works for רבי יהודה, and the other side treats the similar-looking mixture in the plain way.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is a dispute of תנאים': this point is argued over by early sages, so one side cannot prove it.
We follow the majority.
He immersed it in a מקוה.
White wine, which looks similar to water.

steps.whyThisMatters: A proof from one named תנא is weak when another תנא openly disagrees. Here the first opinion of the very same ברייתא gives the other view.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new ברייתא. It is the same one from step 6, quoted again in full to show that רבי יהודה is arguing with someone.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of תנאים;
as it is taught:
A bucket that has in it
white wine or milk,
and he immersed it,
phrases.notes: The bucket is טמא, and he dips it, with what is inside it, into a מקוה.

phrases.english: we follow the majority.
phrases.notes: If most of what is in the bucket is now מקוה water, it works.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: רוֹאִין אוֹתוֹ כְּאִילּוּ הוּא יַיִן אָדוֹם;
phrases.english: we view it as if it were red wine;
if its color would fade, it is fit,
and if not, it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from רבי יהודה made in steps 6–7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof is limited to רבי יהודה's opinion. It does not show a rule everyone agrees to.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The source is a dispute. The first opinion follows the majority and does not imagine the mixture as something different.

steps.title: A contradiction: urine in a bucket is viewed as water
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה about immersing a bucket full of spittle or urine. Its use of 'רואין' for urine will show that the משנה follows רבי יהודה, setting up a contradiction with his 'red wine' rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they raised a contradiction: a bucket that is full of spittle, and he immersed it, it is as if he did not immerse it. Urine: we view it as if it were water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up a contradiction against רבי יהודה's approach by quoting another source. The clash itself is spelled out in steps 10 and 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spittle stays apart from the מקוה water, so the immersion does not count. Urine looks a little different from water, and this source says we 'view it' (רואין) as water. That 'רואין' wording is the clue the גמרא will use to identify the author as רבי יהודה. The actual clash comes with the next case, in steps 10 and 11.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And they contrasted': the גמרא sets one source against another to show a contradiction.
Spittle.
As if he did not immerse; the immersion does not count.
Urine.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
a bucket that is full of spittle,
and he immersed it, it is as if he did not immerse.
Urine,
phrases.notes: This means a bucket full of urine that was immersed.

phrases.english: we view it as if it were water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After limiting the proof to רבי יהודה, the גמרא now raises a contradiction within רבי יהודה's own view, using a משנה that seems to be his.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה's view: his 'red wine' rule in the ברייתא versus the bucket משנה, which uses his 'רואין' language.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The urine clause says 'רואין', which marks the משנה as רבי יהודה's. Yet the same משנה goes on to use a simple majority for מי חטאת instead of his red-wine test.

steps.title: The bucket full of purification water needs a majority of מקוה water
steps.stepSummary: The quoted source ends with its last case. A bucket full of מי חטאת is not purified until the מקוה water becomes more than the מי חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the bucket was full of purification water, it is not purified until the מקוה water becomes more than the purification water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the quote of the bucket source it started in the previous step. This last case is the piece it needs for its challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For urine, the source used the language of 'viewing it' as water. For מי חטאת, it uses a plain counting rule: the מקוה water must outnumber the מי חטאת. That plain majority rule is what will clash with the 'red wine' test of רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Purification water: spring water mixed with the ashes of the פרה אדומה
Until they become more than (until they are the majority)

phrases.english: If it was full of purification water –
phrases.notes: 'It' is the impure bucket from the source quoted in the last step.

phrases.english: it is not purified until the water becomes more
than the purification water.
phrases.notes: 'The water' here means the מקוה water that flows into the bucket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the bucket source begun in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of רבי יהודה's view, since a משנה that uses his 'רואין' language rules by simple majority for מי חטאת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This clause uses a simple majority for מי חטאת, which does not look like רבי יהודה's 'imagine it as red wine' test.

steps.title: The source says 'רואין' like רבי יהודה, yet uses a simple majority
steps.stepSummary: The only one known to hold 'רואין' is רבי יהודה. Yet this same source rules that a majority is enough for מי חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who have we heard holds the idea of 'we view'? רבי יהודה. Yet the source teaches that a majority is enough!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now says its challenge out loud. The source seems to follow רבי יהודה in one case and the חכמים in the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The urine case used the word 'רואין' ('we view'), and that way of thinking belongs to רבי יהודה. For מי חטאת, however, the source does not imagine it as red wine. It just counts the water, like the חכמים, who follow the majority (step 8). One source cannot naturally follow both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We view': we picture the mixture as if it were something else
'Who have you heard holds this?' This is a way to identify which opinion a source follows
It is enough for it
A majority

steps.confusionAlert: The problem is not that 'רואין' and 'majority' always contradict. The problem is that רבי יהודה uses 'רואין' to judge mixtures by the red-wine test, so a plain majority rule in the same source does not sound like him.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard
who holds the idea of 'we view'? –
phrases.notes: This points back to the urine case, which was 'viewed' as if it were water.

phrases.english: רבי יהודה;
phrases.notes: From the ברייתא in steps 6 and 7, where he pictures the liquid as red wine.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches that a majority is enough for it!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאִית לֵיהּ רוֹאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the מי חטאת clause just quoted to state the contradiction outright.
steps.kashyaTarget: The bucket source as a consistent statement of רבי יהודה's view
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'רואין' identifies the author as רבי יהודה, but the majority rule for מי חטאת matches the חכמים and not his red-wine test.

steps.title: אביי begins: this is not a difficulty
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the contradiction is not a real problem. His explanation comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is not difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: This line sets up an answer. אביי announces that the challenge can be solved, and the actual explanation follows in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לא קשיא' tells us the source will not be thrown out. אביי will show how the 'רואין' language and the majority rule can fit together. For now, only his opening words appear.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is not difficult.' This introduces a resolution

phrases.english: Abaye says:
It is not difficult;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the contradiction raised in step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source seems to mix רבי יהודה's 'רואין' with the חכמים' majority rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: אביי claims the two parts can be reconciled. His explanation follows in the next part of the גמרא.
